points.description: States the four ways of passing a pointer to a function: non-constant pointer to constant data, non-constant pointer to non-constant data, constant pointer to constant data, constant pointer to non-constant data (any wording, e.g. 'pointer can/can't change, data can/can't change').
points.partial_credit: Award about 1 mark per correct combination named (up to 4), or 2-3 marks if the answer only gives the general idea that the pointer and/or the data it points to can be constant or non-constant.

rubric.notes: Full marks for naming all four combinations of constant/non-constant pointer with constant/non-constant data, in any wording, however brief. Part marks for naming some of the combinations or for saying only that the pointer and/or the data can be made const. No marks for unrelated answers such as pass by value or reference alone with no mention of const; extra remarks do not cost marks.
